question: Did the planned Ternate Marine Park BMS/BAMS produce a public, fish-specific result attributable to Maragondon River Estuary?

primarySource.title: Achievements in Implementing the Strategic Action Programme in the Philippines during 2008-2021
primarySource.relevantStatement: The evaluation says biodiversity monitoring at Ternate Marine Park was planned for four BMS stations twice a year and BAMS every three years. It supplies no field dates, completed-survey confirmation, station coordinates, fish taxa, or results.
primarySource.interpretation: A monitoring plan is not evidence that monitoring occurred and is not a fish occurrence record.

boundedSearch.outcome: The bounded public web-index search surfaced the same monitoring-plan report and broader Cavite coastal/habitat material, but no completed Ternate Marine Park BMS/BAMS fish-results report explicitly attributable to Maragondon River Estuary.

officialComparisonSource.title: Cavite Ecological Profile 2024
officialComparisonSource.finding: The profile provides provincial coastal-habitat and municipal-fisheries context, but the reviewed/indexed material does not provide fish sampling results crosswalked to Maragondon River Estuary. Province-wide catch labels and named coastal habitat assessments are not reassigned to this estuary.

limits: Search covered public web-indexed material for the listed terms; it did not inspect every LGU/DENR archive, internal database, or unpublished monitoring report.
No report found in this bounded search is not evidence that fish are absent or that monitoring never occurred.
No station, salinity, boundary, catch, or species-level record is inferred from the neighboring Maragondon River fish studies.

nextAction: Request or locate the completed BMS/BAMS field records through an official Ternate Marine Park/PAMO or Cavite PENRO channel. Ask for survey dates, station coordinates and names, methods, fish taxon rank, identification support, report/data license, and whether the records refer to the estuary or another Ternate Marine Park habitat. Do not send a request until separately authorized.
